description: Functions that produce two-dimensional graphics from symbolic functions or from data: Cartesian, logarithmic, parametric, polar, contour, density, vector and complex-valued plots. These are the primary visualization entry points in the Wolfram Language and all share the same option system.

tools.name: Plot
tools.description: Plots one or more symbolic functions of a single real variable over an interval. It adaptively samples the function so that sharp features and singularities are resolved automatically. Use it whenever you have a closed-form expression rather than a list of data points.
tools.usage:
Plot[f, {x, xmin, xmax}]
Plot[{f1, f2, ...}, {x, xmin, xmax}, opts]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Expression (or list of expressions) in the plot variable.

parameters.name: {x, xmin, xmax}
parameters.description: Plot variable and its range.

parameters.name: PlotRange
parameters.description: Vertical range to display; All shows everything, Automatic clips outliers.

parameters.name: PlotStyle
parameters.description: Color/thickness directives, one per curve.

parameters.name: Exclusions
parameters.description: Points or equations where the curve should be broken (poles, branch cuts).

tools.example:
Plot[{Sin[x], Sin[2 x]}, {x, 0, 2 Pi},
  PlotStyle -> {Blue, Red}, PlotLegends -> {"sin x", "sin 2x"},
  Frame -> True, FrameLabel -> {"x", "y"}]
tools.notes: Plot evaluates f symbolically first; wrap the body in Evaluate for held expressions, or use PlotPoints/MaxRecursion for very oscillatory functions. For data use ListPlot or ListLinePlot.

tools.name: ListPlot
tools.description: Plots a list of values or {x, y} pairs as discrete points. Given a flat list, the x coordinates default to 1, 2, 3, .... It is the standard way to display measured or computed data without assuming a functional form.
tools.usage:
ListPlot[{y1, y2, ...}]
ListPlot[{{x1, y1}, {x2, y2}, ...}, opts]
ListPlot[{data1, data2, ...}]

parameters.name: Joined
parameters.description: True connects the points with lines.

parameters.name: PlotMarkers
parameters.description: Markers to draw at each point, e.g. Automatic or "OpenMarkers".

parameters.name: DataRange
parameters.description: x range to assign to a flat list of y values.

tools.example:
data = Table[{x, Sin[x] + RandomReal[{-0.1, 0.1}]}, {x, 0, 2 Pi, 0.1}];
ListPlot[data, PlotMarkers -> Automatic, Frame -> True]
tools.notes: Accepts Association input, TimeSeries objects and QuantityArray. Use ListLinePlot when you always want connected lines.

tools.name: ListLinePlot
tools.description: Plots data as a connected line through the points, equivalent to ListPlot with Joined -> True. Multiple datasets are drawn as separate curves with automatic coloring. Use it for time traces, signals and any sampled curve.
tools.usage:
ListLinePlot[{y1, y2, ...}]
ListLinePlot[{data1, data2, ...}, opts]

parameters.name: InterpolationOrder
parameters.description: 0 gives a step plot, 1 straight segments, 2 or 3 smooth splines.

parameters.name: Filling
parameters.description: Fill under the curve, e.g. Axis, Bottom, or a numeric level.

tools.example:
ListLinePlot[{Accumulate[RandomVariate[NormalDistribution[], 200]],
  Accumulate[RandomVariate[NormalDistribution[], 200]]},
  Filling -> Axis, PlotLegends -> {"walk 1", "walk 2"}]
tools.notes: InterpolationOrder -> 0 is a convenient way to draw staircase/step data; ListStepPlot gives finer control over step placement.

tools.name: LogPlot
tools.description: Plots a function with a logarithmic vertical axis and a linear horizontal axis. Exponential growth or decay appears as a straight line, which makes rate estimation easy. Ticks are labelled with the actual values, not their logarithms.
tools.usage: LogPlot[f, {x, xmin, xmax}, opts]

parameters.name: ScalingFunctions
parameters.description: Override the default scaling, e.g. "Reverse" on an axis.

tools.example: LogPlot[{Exp[x], Exp[2 x], x^3}, {x, 0, 5}, PlotLegends -> "Expressions"]
tools.notes: Non-positive values cannot be shown on a log axis and are dropped. ListLogPlot is the data equivalent.

tools.name: LogLogPlot
tools.description: Plots a function using logarithmic scales on both axes, so power laws appear as straight lines whose slope is the exponent. Use it for scaling studies, spectra and any quantity spanning several decades.
tools.usage: LogLogPlot[f, {x, xmin, xmax}, opts]
tools.example:
LogLogPlot[{x^2, x^3, Sqrt[x]}, {x, 1, 1000}, Frame -> True,
  PlotLegends -> {"x^2", "x^3", "sqrt x"}]
tools.notes: ListLogLogPlot is the data version; fit a line to Log-transformed data with LinearModelFit to recover the exponent.

tools.name: LogLinearPlot
tools.description: Plots a function with a logarithmic horizontal axis and a linear vertical axis. This is the natural choice when the independent variable spans decades, such as frequency in a Bode-style response or concentration in a dose curve.
tools.usage: LogLinearPlot[f, {x, xmin, xmax}, opts]
tools.example:
LogLinearPlot[20 Log10[1/Sqrt[1 + w^2]], {w, 0.01, 100},
  Frame -> True, FrameLabel -> {"omega (rad/s)", "gain (dB)"}]
tools.notes: ListLogLinearPlot handles data. For full control of tick placement use Ticks or FrameTicks with explicit positions.

tools.name: ListLogPlot
tools.description: Plots data on a logarithmic vertical axis. It accepts the same data forms as ListPlot, including pairs, associations and time series. Use it to inspect exponential trends in measurements.
tools.usage:
ListLogPlot[{y1, y2, ...}, opts]
ListLogPlot[{{x1, y1}, ...}, Joined -> True]
tools.example:
ListLogPlot[Table[{n, 2^n}, {n, 1, 20}], Joined -> True,
  PlotMarkers -> Automatic]
tools.notes: Related: ListLogLogPlot and ListLogLinearPlot for the other scalings.

tools.name: ParametricPlot
tools.description: Plots a curve or a filled region defined by parametric coordinate functions. With one parameter it draws a curve; with two parameters it draws the image of a rectangle under the map, which is useful for visualizing coordinate transformations. Adaptive sampling handles loops and cusps.
tools.usage:
ParametricPlot[{fx, fy}, {t, tmin, tmax}]
ParametricPlot[{fx, fy}, {u, umin, umax}, {v, vmin, vmax}]

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: Draw parameter mesh lines on the image region.

parameters.name: PlotRange
parameters.description: Region of the plane to display.

tools.example:
ParametricPlot[{Cos[3 t] Cos[t], Cos[3 t] Sin[t]}, {t, 0, Pi},
  AspectRatio -> 1, Axes -> False]
tools.notes: For 3D curves and surfaces use ParametricPlot3D. PolarPlot is a convenient special case for r(theta).

tools.name: PolarPlot
tools.description: Plots a curve given in polar form as radius r as a function of the angle theta. Several radial functions can be plotted together. Use it for antenna patterns, roses, limacons and any naturally angular data.
tools.usage:
PolarPlot[r, {theta, thetamin, thetamax}, opts]
PolarPlot[{r1, r2, ...}, {theta, tmin, tmax}]

parameters.name: PolarAxes
parameters.description: Whether to draw polar axes (True/False).

parameters.name: PolarGridLines
parameters.description: Radial and angular grid lines.

tools.example:
PolarPlot[{1 + Cos[t], 1 + Cos[2 t]}, {t, 0, 2 Pi},
  PolarAxes -> True, PolarGridLines -> Automatic]
tools.notes: ListPolarPlot plots {theta, r} pairs. Negative r values are plotted in the opposite direction.

tools.name: ListPolarPlot
tools.description: Plots data in polar coordinates from a list of radii or {theta, r} pairs. With a flat list the angles are spread uniformly over 2 Pi. Useful for directional measurements such as wind roses or beam patterns.
tools.usage:
ListPolarPlot[{r1, r2, ...}]
ListPolarPlot[{{t1, r1}, {t2, r2}, ...}, Joined -> True]
tools.example:
ListPolarPlot[Table[{t, 1 + 0.3 Sin[5 t]}, {t, 0, 2 Pi, 0.05}],
  Joined -> True, PolarAxes -> True]

tools.name: ContourPlot
tools.description: Draws contour lines of a function of two variables, or the solution set of an equation. Contours are shaded between levels by default, giving an immediate sense of the landscape. Give an equation lhs == rhs to draw an implicit curve instead.
tools.usage:
ContourPlot[f, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}]
ContourPlot[lhs == rhs, {x, ...}, {y, ...}]

parameters.name: Contours
parameters.description: Number of contours or an explicit list of levels.

parameters.name: ContourShading
parameters.description: None for line-only contours, or a color function.

parameters.name: PlotPoints
parameters.description: Initial sampling density; raise it for fine structure.

tools.example:
ContourPlot[Sin[x] Cos[y], {x, -3, 3}, {y, -3, 3},
  Contours -> 15, ContourShading -> Automatic, PlotLegends -> Automatic]
tools.notes: ContourPlot can plot several equations at once as a list. For sampled data use ListContourPlot.

tools.name: DensityPlot
tools.description: Draws a function of two variables as a smoothly shaded density image, with color mapping the function value. It gives a continuous view where ContourPlot gives discrete levels. Combine with Mesh -> None for a clean heat-map look.
tools.usage: DensityPlot[f, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}, opts]

parameters.name: ColorFunction
parameters.description: Named gradient such as "TemperatureMap" or a pure function.

parameters.name: ColorFunctionScaling
parameters.description: False to pass raw values to ColorFunction.

tools.example:
DensityPlot[Sin[x y], {x, -3, 3}, {y, -3, 3},
  ColorFunction -> "SunsetColors", PlotLegends -> Automatic, PlotPoints -> 60]
tools.notes: ListDensityPlot handles arrays and point data; ArrayPlot is faster for pure matrices.

tools.name: RegionPlot
tools.description: Shades the two-dimensional region where an inequality or logical combination of inequalities is True. It is the direct way to visualize feasible sets, domains of definition and constraint intersections. Multiple regions can be drawn together and styled separately.
tools.usage:
RegionPlot[pred, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}]
RegionPlot[{pred1, pred2}, {x, ...}, {y, ...}]

parameters.name: BoundaryStyle
parameters.description: Style of the region boundary curve.

parameters.name: PlotPoints
parameters.description: Sampling density; increase for thin or spiky regions.

tools.example:
RegionPlot[x^2 + y^2 < 1 && y > x^2 - 0.5, {x, -1.5, 1.5}, {y, -1.5, 1.5},
  BoundaryStyle -> Directive[Thick, Black]]
tools.notes: RegionPlot also accepts symbolic regions such as Disk[] or ImplicitRegion. Use RegionPlot3D for volumes.

tools.name: StreamPlot
tools.description: Draws streamlines of a two-dimensional vector field, showing the paths a particle would follow. Arrowheads indicate direction and line density indicates where the field is sampled. Use it for flow fields, phase portraits of ODE systems and electromagnetic fields.
tools.usage: StreamPlot[{vx, vy}, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}, opts]

parameters.name: StreamPoints
parameters.description: Number, seed points, or Fine/Coarse control of streamline placement.

parameters.name: StreamStyle
parameters.description: Style or arrow shape for the streamlines.

parameters.name: StreamColorFunction
parameters.description: Color streamlines by magnitude or a supplied scalar.

tools.example:
StreamPlot[{y, -x - 0.3 y}, {x, -3, 3}, {y, -3, 3},
  StreamColorFunction -> "Rainbow", Frame -> True]
tools.notes: StreamDensityPlot overlays a density background; ListStreamPlot works from sampled vector data.

tools.name: VectorPlot
tools.description: Draws a field of arrows representing a two-dimensional vector field on a regular grid. Arrow length and color encode magnitude by default. It complements StreamPlot when you want local direction and strength rather than trajectories.
tools.usage: VectorPlot[{vx, vy}, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}, opts]

parameters.name: VectorPoints
parameters.description: Grid density or explicit sample points.

parameters.name: VectorScaling
parameters.description: How arrow length maps to magnitude, e.g. "Linear".

parameters.name: VectorColorFunction
parameters.description: Color arrows by magnitude or another scalar.

tools.example:
VectorPlot[{-y, x}/Sqrt[x^2 + y^2 + 0.1], {x, -2, 2}, {y, -2, 2},
  VectorPoints -> 15, VectorColorFunction -> Hue]
tools.notes: VectorDensityPlot adds a scalar density background; ListVectorPlot takes an array of vectors.

tools.name: VectorDensityPlot
tools.description: Combines a vector-field arrow plot with a background density plot of a scalar function. This shows, for example, a flow field on top of a pressure field in one picture. The scalar defaults to the vector magnitude if only two components are given.
tools.usage: VectorDensityPlot[{{vx, vy}, s}, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}]
tools.example:
VectorDensityPlot[{{-y, x}, x^2 + y^2}, {x, -2, 2}, {y, -2, 2},
  ColorFunction -> "TemperatureMap"]
tools.notes: StreamDensityPlot is the streamline analogue.

tools.name: StreamDensityPlot
tools.description: Draws streamlines of a vector field over a shaded density background of an associated scalar field. Use it when both the flow direction and an accompanying scalar such as speed or potential matter. It accepts all StreamPlot and DensityPlot options.
tools.usage: StreamDensityPlot[{{vx, vy}, s}, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}]
tools.example: StreamDensityPlot[{{y, -Sin[x]}, y^2/2 - Cos[x]}, {x, -Pi, Pi}, {y, -3, 3}]

tools.name: ListContourPlot
tools.description: Generates contour lines from an array of values or from scattered {x, y, z} triples. Scattered data is interpolated onto a mesh automatically. Use it for gridded measurements, simulation output or survey data.
tools.usage:
ListContourPlot[array]
ListContourPlot[{{x1, y1, z1}, ...}, opts]

parameters.name: InterpolationOrder
parameters.description: Order of interpolation used between samples.

parameters.name: DataRange
parameters.description: Coordinate range that the array spans.

tools.example:
data = Table[Sin[x] Cos[y], {x, -3, 3, 0.1}, {y, -3, 3, 0.1}];
ListContourPlot[data, DataRange -> {{-3, 3}, {-3, 3}}, PlotLegends -> Automatic]

tools.name: ListDensityPlot
tools.description: Draws a shaded density plot from an array of values or scattered triples, interpolating as needed. It is the data counterpart of DensityPlot and accepts the same color options. Use it for heat maps of measured fields.
tools.usage:
ListDensityPlot[array, opts]
ListDensityPlot[{{x, y, f}, ...}, opts]
tools.notes: For an exact pixel-per-element rendering of a matrix use ArrayPlot or MatrixPlot instead.

tools.name: ListVectorPlot
tools.description: Plots a vector field given as an array of {vx, vy} pairs on a grid, or as a list of {{x, y}, {vx, vy}} records. Vectors are resampled and drawn as arrows. Use it for measured or simulated flow data.
tools.usage:
ListVectorPlot[array]
ListVectorPlot[{{{x, y}, {vx, vy}}, ...}, opts]
tools.example:
field = Table[{-y, x}, {y, -2, 2, 0.4}, {x, -2, 2, 0.4}];
ListVectorPlot[field, VectorColorFunction -> "Rainbow"]

tools.name: ListStreamPlot
tools.description: Draws streamlines through a vector field supplied as data rather than as a formula. The field is interpolated before the streamlines are integrated. Use it for CFD output, weather data or particle-image velocimetry results.
tools.usage:
ListStreamPlot[array, opts]
ListStreamPlot[{{{x, y}, {vx, vy}}, ...}, opts]
tools.example:
field = Table[{Sin[y], Cos[x]}, {y, -3, 3, 0.3}, {x, -3, 3, 0.3}];
ListStreamPlot[field, StreamPoints -> Fine]

tools.name: DiscretePlot
tools.description: Plots the values of an expression at a discrete sequence of integer or stepped arguments, drawing stems from the axis by default. Use it for sequences, sampled signals and combinatorial quantities where the discreteness matters. The filling and marker can be styled independently.
tools.usage:
DiscretePlot[expr, {n, nmax}]
DiscretePlot[expr, {n, nmin, nmax, dn}, opts]

parameters.name: ExtentSize
parameters.description: Draw bars of a given width instead of stems.

parameters.name: PlotMarkers
parameters.description: Marker drawn at the top of each stem.

tools.example:
DiscretePlot[Sin[n]/n, {n, 1, 30}, Filling -> Axis,
  PlotMarkers -> Automatic]
tools.notes: DiscretePlot3D is the 3D analogue. For a plain stem look of existing data use ListPlot with Filling -> Axis.

tools.name: ListStepPlot
tools.description: Plots data as a piecewise-constant step function, with control over whether each value applies before, after or centered on its x position. It is the right choice for cumulative distributions, sampled-and-held signals and counting processes. Steps can be filled to the axis.
tools.usage:
ListStepPlot[{y1, y2, ...}]
ListStepPlot[data, Center|Left|Right, opts]
tools.example:
ListStepPlot[Accumulate[RandomInteger[{0, 1}, 40]], Center,
  Filling -> Axis, Frame -> True]
tools.notes: ListLinePlot with InterpolationOrder -> 0 gives a similar result with less control over step alignment.

tools.name: StackedListPlot
tools.description: Plots several datasets stacked on top of one another so that the top curve shows the running total. Each layer is filled, making part-to-whole evolution easy to read. Use it for composition over time, such as resource usage by category.
tools.usage: StackedListPlot[{data1, data2, ...}, opts]
tools.example:
StackedListPlot[{Range[10], Reverse[Range[10]], ConstantArray[3, 10]},
  PlotLegends -> {"a", "b", "c"}]
tools.notes: StackedDateListPlot is the dated version. Pass ScalingFunctions -> "Percent" style options via PlotLayout -> "Percentile" for normalized stacks.

tools.name: DateListPlot
tools.description: Plots values against dates or times, labelling the horizontal axis with calendar-aware ticks. It accepts DateObject pairs, TimeSeries objects and absolute time numbers. Use it for any chronological series where readable date ticks matter.
tools.usage:
DateListPlot[{{date1, y1}, {date2, y2}, ...}, opts]
DateListPlot[timeseries, opts]

parameters.name: DateTicksFormat
parameters.description: Format specification for the date axis labels.

parameters.name: PlotRange
parameters.description: Can be given as a date range, e.g. {{2020, 1, 1}, {2021, 1, 1}}.

tools.notes: DateListLogPlot and StackedDateListPlot are related; DateListStepPlot exists for step-style dated data.

tools.name: DateListLogPlot
tools.description: Plots dated data with a logarithmic vertical axis, keeping calendar ticks horizontally. Use it for quantities that grow multiplicatively over time, such as case counts or compounding balances. It accepts the same data forms as DateListPlot.
tools.usage: DateListLogPlot[{{date, y}, ...}, opts]
tools.example:
DateListLogPlot[Table[{DateObject[{2024, 1, n}], 2^n}, {n, 1, 20}],
  Joined -> True]

tools.name: StackedDateListPlot
tools.description: Stacks several dated series so the layers sum to the total at each date. It combines the date axis handling of DateListPlot with the cumulative layering of StackedListPlot. Use it for revenue, traffic or energy mix by category over time.
tools.usage: StackedDateListPlot[{series1, series2, ...}, opts]
tools.example:
d = DateRange[DateObject[{2024, 1, 1}], DateObject[{2024, 1, 20}]];
StackedDateListPlot[{Thread[{d, Range[20]}], Thread[{d, Reverse@Range[20]}]}]

tools.name: ComplexPlot
tools.description: Plots a complex-valued function over a region of the complex plane, using hue for the argument and brightness for the magnitude. Zeros appear as dark points and poles as bright points, with the color wheel order revealing multiplicity. It is the fastest way to see the global structure of an analytic function.
tools.usage: ComplexPlot[f, {z, zmin, zmax}, opts]

parameters.name: ColorFunction
parameters.description: Named complex color scheme such as "CyclicLogAbsArg".

parameters.name: PlotLegends
parameters.description: Automatic adds a color wheel legend.

tools.example:
ComplexPlot[(z^2 - 1)/(z^2 + 1), {z, -2 - 2 I, 2 + 2 I},
  PlotLegends -> Automatic]
tools.notes: ComplexPlot3D shows magnitude as height with argument as color. ComplexArrayPlot does the same for arrays of complex numbers.

tools.name: ComplexContourPlot
tools.description: Draws contours in the complex plane of a real-valued function of a complex variable, or the solution curves of a complex equation. Use it to visualize level sets of Abs, Re, Im or Arg of an analytic function. It accepts the usual contour styling options.
tools.usage:
ComplexContourPlot[f, {z, zmin, zmax}, opts]
ComplexContourPlot[lhs == rhs, {z, zmin, zmax}]
tools.example: ComplexContourPlot[Abs[z^3 - 1], {z, -2 - 2 I, 2 + 2 I}, Contours -> 20]

tools.name: ComplexStreamPlot
tools.description: Draws streamlines of the vector field associated with a complex function, treating the real and imaginary parts as field components. This visualizes potential flows and conformal maps. ComplexVectorPlot gives the same field as arrows.
tools.usage: ComplexStreamPlot[f, {z, zmin, zmax}, opts]
tools.example: ComplexStreamPlot[Conjugate[1/z], {z, -2 - 2 I, 2 + 2 I}, StreamPoints -> Fine]
tools.notes: Use Conjugate[f] to get the physical flow field of a complex potential.

tools.name: ComplexVectorPlot
tools.description: Plots a complex function as a field of arrows in the complex plane, with each arrow giving the value at that point. It makes rotation and scaling behaviour of a map immediately visible. Use together with ComplexPlot for a full picture.
tools.usage: ComplexVectorPlot[f, {z, zmin, zmax}, opts]
tools.example: ComplexVectorPlot[z^2, {z, -1.5 - 1.5 I, 1.5 + 1.5 I}, VectorPoints -> 12]

tools.name: ComplexArrayPlot
tools.description: Renders an array of complex numbers as an image using hue for argument and lightness for magnitude. It is the array analogue of ComplexPlot and is very fast for large matrices. Use it to inspect FFT output, transfer matrices or wavefunctions.
tools.usage: ComplexArrayPlot[array, opts]
tools.example:
ComplexArrayPlot[Fourier[Table[Exp[-((i - 32)^2 + (j - 32)^2)/100.],
   {i, 64}, {j, 64}]], PlotLegends -> Automatic]

tools.name: ReImPlot
tools.description: Plots the real and imaginary parts of a complex-valued function of a real variable as two curves on the same axes. It avoids having to write Re and Im wrappers and keeps consistent styling and a legend. Use it for signals, transfer functions and solutions of complex ODEs.
tools.usage: ReImPlot[f, {x, xmin, xmax}, opts]

parameters.name: ReImStyle
parameters.description: Styles for the real and imaginary curves.

parameters.name: ReImLabels
parameters.description: Labels used in the legend.

tools.example: ReImPlot[Exp[I x] /(1 + I x), {x, -10, 10}, PlotLegends -> Automatic]

tools.name: AbsArgPlot
tools.description: Plots the magnitude of a complex-valued function of a real variable, coloring the curve by its argument. It is the polar counterpart of ReImPlot. Use it when phase behaviour along a real parameter is important, as in frequency responses.
tools.usage: AbsArgPlot[f, {x, xmin, xmax}, opts]
tools.example: AbsArgPlot[1/(1 + I x)^3, {x, -5, 5}, PlotLegends -> Automatic]

tools.name: NumberLinePlot
tools.description: Plots points, intervals and regions on a one-dimensional number line. It accepts numbers, Interval objects, inequalities and symbolic regions. Use it to show solution sets, tolerance bands or sample positions compactly.
tools.usage:
NumberLinePlot[{v1, v2, ...}]
NumberLinePlot[pred, {x, xmin, xmax}]
tools.example: NumberLinePlot[{Interval[{-2, 1}], 3, x^2 < 4 && x > -1}, {x, -5, 5}]
